findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported in Salesforce CalendarService
findings.body: `getClient()` now calls `prisma.credential.update({...})`, but the file imports no Prisma client (only `getLocation`, `WEBAPP_URL`, `HttpError`, `logger`, types, `getAppKeysFromSlug`, `parseRefreshTokenResponse`). `prisma` is therefore an undefined identifier: TypeScript type-check/build will fail, and at runtime every instantiation of `SalesforceCalendarService` throws a `ReferenceError`, breaking all Salesforce bookings. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

findings.title: Google credential key is overwritten with a Zod safeParse result wrapper
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse()` returns the raw `safeParse` result (`{ success: true, data: {...} }`), not the parsed object, yet the return value is written straight into the DB: `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema); await prisma.credential.update({ ..., data: { key } })`. Previously the code stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)`. After this change the stored credential key becomes `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`, so the next `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` fails and the user's Google Calendar credential is permanently broken. The value should be `...data` (and the helper should return the parsed data, not the wrapper).

findings.title: minimumTokenResponseSchema is not a valid schema and silently strips all token fields
findings.body: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both stringify a ZodType object to the same literal key (`"[object Object]"`), so the schema is effectively `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]": unknown }`. It therefore (a) never validates that an expiry field exists, despite the comment, and (b) because Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, the returned `data` contains only `access_token` — `refresh_token`, `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, `scope`, `instance_url`, `api_domain`, etc. are discarded. Any caller that persists this data (Google, Office365, Zoom) loses the fields it needs: e.g. Zoom computes `expiry_date = Date.now() + undefined * 1000` → `NaN`, after which `isTokenValid` never triggers a refresh again. Use an explicit schema such as `z.object({ access_token: z.string(), expires_in: z.number().optional(), expiry_date: z.number().optional() }).passthrough()`.

findings.title: Placeholder string overwrites a valid refresh token
findings.body: `if (!refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token) refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token";` injects the literal string `"refresh_token"` whenever the provider response omits a refresh token — and it does this unconditionally, even when credential sharing is disabled. In `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` the result is merged into the stored key (`{ ...o365AuthCredentials, ...tokenResponse.data }`) and `refresh_token` is optional in `refreshTokenResponseSchema`, so a refresh response without a new refresh token will replace the user's real Microsoft refresh token with the garbage value, permanently breaking that credential. Only fill in a placeholder when the credential-sync path is active, and never let it clobber an existing refresh token.

findings.title: Sync endpoint returns a fetch Response where callers expect axios/SDK response shapes
findings.body: When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, this helper always returns a `fetch` `Response`, but several call sites expect the shape their original client returned: `zoho-bigin` and `zohocrm` read `tokenInfo.data.error` / `tokenInfo.data.access_token` (axios), `hubspot` expects a `HubspotToken` object with `accessToken`/`expiresIn`, and `googlecalendar` reads `res?.data`. With sync enabled these all dereference `undefined` (TypeError, or `NaN` expiry and `setAccessToken(undefined)`), so token refresh fails exactly in the mode this PR adds. The helper needs to normalise the response per app (e.g. return parsed JSON and have each caller adapt) rather than leaking two different return types.

findings.title: Credential sync request carries no authentication and its status is never checked
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` with no shared secret, signature, or auth header, so the self-hoster's endpoint has no way to verify the caller; anyone who learns the URL can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user ids. The inbound direction (`/api/webhook/app-credential`) does use `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, so the asymmetry is clearly unintended. Additionally, `response.ok` is never checked, so a 4xx/5xx HTML error body is passed on to the per-app parsing code, producing confusing downstream failures instead of a clear error.

findings.title: Credential id passed where the user id is expected in Zoho Bigin refresh
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(fn, "zoho-bigin", credentialId)` passes `credentialId` as the third argument, but that parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. With credential sharing enabled the self-hoster's endpoint will be asked for the tokens of whatever user happens to have id == credential id, i.e. the wrong user's credentials get fetched and stored (potential cross-account token leak). `refreshAccessToken` must receive and forward `credential.userId`.

findings.title: Wrong app slug ("zoomvideo") sent to the credential sync endpoint
findings.body: `refreshOAuthTokens(..., "zoomvideo", credential.userId)` uses the app's directory name, not its slug. The Zoom app's slug is `zoom` (see `zoomvideo/api/callback.ts`, which creates the credential with `appId: "zoom"`, and the `App.slug` row used by the new `/api/webhook/app-credential` endpoint). A self-hoster's endpoint keyed on the Cal.com app slug will not recognise `zoomvideo`, so Zoom token sync silently fails.

findings.title: appStoreMetadata is indexed by slug, but it is keyed by app dirName
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata[app.slug as keyof typeof appStoreMetadata]` casts the slug to a key of the generated metadata map, which is keyed by app directory name. For every app whose dirName differs from its slug — `googlecalendar`/`google-calendar`, `office365calendar`/`office365-calendar`, `zoomvideo`/`zoom`, `office365video`/`msteams` — the lookup returns `undefined` and the handler responds 404 "App not found. Ensure that you have the correct app slug". Those are precisely the apps this feature targets, so the webhook is unusable for them. Resolve the metadata via a slug lookup (e.g. `getAppFromSlug`) or by the app's `dirName`.

findings.title: Unvalidated input and decryption errors surface as unhandled 500s
findings.body: `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` throws a `ZodError` for a malformed payload, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, ...))` throws when the key is wrong or the ciphertext/JSON is invalid. Neither is caught, so callers get an opaque 500 (with a stack trace in the server logs and, in dev, the response) instead of a 400 with an actionable message, making integration debugging hard for self-hosters. Use `safeParse` plus a try/catch around decryption and return 400.

findings.title: No HTTP method restriction and non-constant-time secret comparison
findings.body: The handler accepts any HTTP method (GET, DELETE, …) and compares the webhook secret with `!==` on the raw header value. A method guard (`POST` only) prevents accidental credential writes from GET/prefetch traffic, and `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on equal-length buffers avoids leaking the secret through response-time differences on a write-capable, unauthenticated-by-default endpoint.

findings.title: Custom webhook header name is case-sensitive
findings.body: `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"]` relies on the operator configuring the name in lowercase, because Node lowercases incoming header names. If a self-hoster sets `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME="Calcom-Webhook-Secret"` the lookup yields `undefined` and every request is rejected with "Invalid webhook secret" with no hint why. Apply `.toLowerCase()` to the configured name instead of relying on the .env comment.

findings.title: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED evaluates to the encryption key, not a boolean
findings.body: `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` returns the value of `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when both are set, so this exported "flag" is actually the secret string. `packages/lib/constants.ts` is imported broadly (including from client-reachable modules), so any place that logs or serialises this constant leaks the AES key. Wrap it in `!!(...)` so only a boolean is exported.

findings.title: Salesforce token is refreshed on every instantiation and the stale token is still used
findings.body: `getClient()` is called from the constructor and now unconditionally POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` with `grant_type=refresh_token`, regardless of whether the stored access token is still valid — an extra Salesforce round trip (and API-limit consumption) for every service construction, e.g. on each availability/booking path. Worse, after refreshing and persisting the new token the returned `jsforce.Connection` is still built with `accessToken: credentialKey.access_token` and `instanceUrl: credentialKey.instance_url` from the old key, so the freshly obtained token is discarded and requests may run with an expired token. Gate the refresh on expiry and build the connection from the refreshed values. (Note the `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` branch below is dead code, since `parseRefreshTokenResponse` already throws on failure.)

findings.title: Token refresh success detected via `statusText === "OK"`
findings.body: `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` is unreliable: `statusText` is an empty string for HTTP/2 responses (undici) and may carry other reason phrases for 2xx responses, so a successful refresh can be rejected with an empty error message while a non-2xx body could slip through. Check `response.ok` / `response.status` instead.

findings.title: Apps wired to refreshOAuthTokens still validate with provider-specific strict schemas
findings.body: Webex (and likewise `larkcalendar` via `handleLarkError`, `office365video`, `hubspot`, `zohocrm`, `zoho-bigin`) now call `refreshOAuthTokens`, but still parse the result with the provider's own strict contract — here `webexRefreshedTokenSchema` requires `refresh_token`, a literal `scope` of `"spark:kms meeting:schedules_read meeting:schedules_write"` and `token_type: "Bearer"`. The documented sync-endpoint contract ("The response should only contain the access token and expiry date") cannot satisfy these schemas, so with credential sharing enabled refresh fails ("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned") or yields `NaN` expiry dates. These call sites need to go through `parseRefreshTokenResponse` (once it is fixed) or the feature should be documented as unsupported for them.

findings.title: Webhook silently overwrites one of several credentials for the same user and app
findings.body: The upsert uses `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })`. Users can legitimately have more than one credential for the same app (e.g. two Google Calendar accounts); the webhook will overwrite whichever row is returned first and leave the others stale, with no indication to the caller. The payload has no way to target a specific credential, so consider including an external identifier/account email in the schema or documenting the single-credential-per-app assumption.

findings.title: No tests for the new credential-sync webhook or token parsing helper
findings.body: The PR adds an unauthenticated-by-default write endpoint that creates/updates OAuth credentials plus a shared `parseRefreshTokenResponse`/`refreshOAuthTokens` layer used by ~10 apps, with no unit or integration tests. Given that the helpers currently mis-handle schemas and return types (see other findings), at minimum there should be tests covering: rejected requests when sharing is disabled / secret mismatch, slug→metadata resolution for apps whose dirName differs from the slug, credential create vs update, and that `parseRefreshTokenResponse` preserves `refresh_token`/expiry in both sharing modes.
